facts: A project toolchain often declares more packages than one job uses, and env and exec compose the whole set by default. [L6]
Without lazy mode, every declared package downloads before the job's first command starts. [L6]
Lazy mode changes when content downloads, not what is composed; declared names still resolve and which still finds the package. [L8]
Under always, package bytes stay unfetched until the first invocation of one of the package's names. [L8]
Every env-composing command accepts the lazy-mode flag. [L12]
The shell example shows how a shim is composed with lazy mode. [L14]
The cast example shows cmake being deferred until its first use. [L16]
Under always, OCX writes a generated launcher per declared name into a shim directory placed on PATH in the eager entrypoints slot. [L18]
The which command and the pull JSON report tag each entry as package or shim, so scripts need no filesystem probing. [L18]
Analogy: containerd's stargz snapshotter lazily fetches files per file, while OCX does it per package on first invocation. [L20]
Lazy mode is a policy resolved through five tiers, with never as the eager floor. [L26]
Tier 1 is the lazy-mode flag on the invoked command. [L30]
Tier 2 is a package entry in ocx.toml. [L31]
Tier 3 is a group entry in ocx.toml. [L32]
Tier 4 is the toolchain-level lazy-mode key in ocx.toml. [L33]
Tier 5 is the OCX_LAZY_MODE environment variable. [L34]
The floor is never, meaning eager materialization. [L35]
Each tier is optional, and an absent tier inherits from the next one down rather than meaning never. [L37]
A package-tier never overrides a toolchain-level always for that one package, so it composes eagerly while others defer. [L37]
When a package sits in several groups, pull materializes it eagerly if any of those groups resolves to never. [L39]
The generated launcher is a small script, deliberately similar to the one an entry point writes. [L43]
The shell example shows the generated shim body, which execs the hidden launcher shim subcommand with the pinned identifier. [L45]
The launcher runs the ordinary pull, then resolves the requested name on the package PATH and executes it. [L51]
A lazily materialized package is byte-identical to the same package installed eagerly. [L51]
Once materialized, the real entrypoints outrank the shim on PATH, so later calls never re-trigger the shim. [L53]
The which command reports kind shim before first use and package after. [L53]
The lazy-report setting controls progress for the first-invocation download and resolves inside the shim process itself. [L57]
Lazy-report cannot be a flag on env or exec, because the shim process is separate from the composing command. [L57]
Lazy-report tier 1 is a flag accepted only by the hidden launcher shim subcommand, never typed by users. [L61]
Lazy-report tier 2 is a package entry in ocx.toml. [L62]
Lazy-report tier 3 is the toolchain-level lazy-report key in ocx.toml. [L63]
Lazy-report tier 4 is the OCX_LAZY_REPORT environment variable. [L64]
The lazy-report floor is silent, one tier shorter than lazy-mode because no group applies after composition. [L65]
Progress opens a channel on the controlling terminal, and an invocation that finds the package already stored opens nothing. [L67]
Where no terminal exists, progress silently degrades to silent instead of failing, and errors always reach stderr. [L67]
Some metadata shapes need content on disk to substitute, so a shim cannot detect them the way an eager install does. [L71]
Env and package env then emit a warning-only advisories array in JSON output, and never fail composition. [L71]
On Windows the deferred slot is name.exe, hardlinked from the shared shim blob, paired with a name.shimref sidecar. [L75]
The sidecar holds one line naming the pinned identifier, and lazy-mode composes the same way on Windows as elsewhere. [L75]
First invocation on Windows reads the sidecar and materializes the package through the same launcher shim pipeline. [L77]
A shim directory is kept alive by the same lock-pinned root set that keeps an eager package alive. [L81]
The clean --force command collects every shim directory, because a deferred package has no install symlink. [L83]
The first invocation after clean --force re-materializes the deferred package from scratch. [L83]
